newsitem.title: USA: AOL reports big quarterly loss, revenues higher.
newsitem.headline: AOL reports big quarterly loss, revenues higher.

text.p: America Online Inc. said Thursday it lost $11.8 million in its fiscal fourth quarter due mainly to one-time charges, but membership and advertising gains padded the company's revenues.
AOL, the world's largest Internet online service, reported a loss of $11.8 million, or 12 cents a share, for the period, compared with earnings of $16.1 million, or 14 cents a share, a year earlier.

The Dulles, Va.-based company said the net loss resulted from moving a $25.7 million charge for "information provider termination expenses" from the second quarter to the fourth quarter and from restating $7.3 million in third quarter operating results.
Excluding the special items, AOL earned $10.9 million in the quarter, or 9 cents a share, edging out analysts' average estimate of 7 cents a share compiled by First Call.

Revenues jumped by 42 percent to a record $475.7 million from $334.5 million a year ago. The company credited strong growth in membership and advertising, commerce and transaction revenues, cost-savings and improved member retention.
AOL said it added 600,000 net new members in the quarter, bringing its total membership to 8,636,000 worldwide as of June 30, 1997.
It said it surpassed 750,000 members internationally during the fiscal fourth quarter, a year and a half after launching its first overseas service in Germany.
AOL's stock edged up 12.5 cents to end at $71 on the New York Stock Exchange.
